title: ‘Most important strategic partner’: Mercedes’ Nvidia self-driving deal
key_facts: Mercedes-Benz will develop its next generation of driver assistance and automated driving systems with Nvidia, the two companies said on Friday 16 Oct 2026; the announcement came a day after Volvo Cars expanded its own Nvidia partnership.
Both carmakers build on the same Nvidia stack: the Hyperion computer and sensor architecture, the Alpamayo driving software and the Halos safety system.
Mercedes' MB.OS operating system will work with Hyperion's in-car computer and sensors; the systems support future SAE Level 4 uses, including robolimousines.
At Level 4, a car drives itself without a human taking over, within set conditions.
Jörg Burzer, Mercedes-Benz's chief technology officer, called Nvidia "our most important strategic partner in automated driving".

Mercedes says urban point-to-point navigation is due in selected German cities by the end of 2026; in September, London-based Wayve signed a deal to put its AI Driver in future Mercedes cars within two years.
Neither carmaker gave a launch date or said which models will get the systems first; Mercedes framed its plans as covering the next decade.

notes: Joint company announcement relayed by The Next Web; no doubts about the facts, the open point is timing.
